subject: Request: Packaging network segregation evidence for SIG/CAIQ
messages:
From: security@acme-fin.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: audits@thirdparty-assess.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ ask — Dedicated & Private network diagrams and isolation artifacts

Hi Kimberly,

We are preparing for our SIG assessment and Acme's security team has a few outstanding asks specific to Redwood's Dedicated and Private deployment isolation model. Can you provide the following artifacts (or point us to the canonical packaged evidence) by end of week: 

- Network diagrams that clearly show: control plane vs data plane separation for Dedicated & Private, ingress/egress choke points, KMS boundaries, and any optional airgap/edge variants.
- A short narrative (1 page) describing tenant separation, KV cache isolation, and how routing policies enforce tenancy in Private deployments.
- A list/index of SIG/CAIQ evidence items (mapping: question ID -> file) and any redaction guidance.
- Any SOC 2/PCI call-outs that materially change the network posture (e.g., daytime maintenance windows that bypass certain routing).

We have a tight window for the assessment — ideally a consolidated packet by Friday (2026-07-31). If you need to stage deliverables, please commit to a first drop (diagrams + index) and a follow-up with detailed narratives.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Senior Security Manager
Acme Financial
security@acme-fin.com

Attachments: none
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: security@acme-fin.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ ask — Dedicated & Private network diagrams and isolation artifacts

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list.

We can absolutely deliver a staged packet. Proposed plan: 

1) First drop (by 2026-07-30 EOD): updated network diagram set (control/data plane overlays for Dedicated & Private), an evidence index mapping SIG/CAIQ QIDs to artifacts, and a redaction guide. See attached index stub (sig-evidence-index.pdf) and a diagram preview (network-diagram-v3.png).

2) Second drop (by 2026-08-04): one-page narratives for tenancy isolation, KV cache handling, routing policy enforcement, and any SOC 2 call-outs; plus the segregation checklist spreadsheet for internal/third-party review.

A couple of clarifying items so we package what you need: 
- Do you want an explicit variant that depicts an on-premises Private deployment (air-gapped) vs VPC-connected Private? We can include both; the on-prem map will add a day for redaction.
- For the SOC 2/PCI call-outs, are you asking for policy-level statements (e.g., scheduled maintenance exception procedures) or operational evidence (runbooks/change tickets)?

If that timeline works, we'll push the first drop to the Drive link and attach the index and a diagram preview here.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: sig-evidence-index.pdf, network-diagram-v3.png
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, security@acme-fin.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ ask — Dedicated & Private network diagrams and isolation artifacts

Looping in technical detail per Kimberly's plan. Quick notes for Acme to confirm scope: 

- Variants: we will include two diagram variants — (A) Hosted/Dedicated (shared control plane w/ tenant-isolated inference pools) and (B) Private (customer VPC or on-prem package). The Private variant will show optional airgap and a VPC peering option.

- Control/data plane separation: control plane (management APIs, model catalog, billing telemetry) always runs in the Redwood control region (multi-tenant control plane) and is logically separated via RBAC, KMS scoping, and auth tokens. Data plane (model inference GPU pools) for Dedicated can be colocated in customer-dedicated pools; for Private it may be provisioned inside customer VPC or on-prem enclave — diagrams will annotate KMS boundary and egress chokepoints.

- Tenant isolation specifics: KV cache isolation is enforced per-deployment instance (separate process-level memory spaces and namespaces). Batching infrastructure enforces tenant-aware batch grouping; fallback policies never mix tenant requests across isolation boundaries. We'll include a one-page diagram showing cache key namespace partitioning.

- Evidence mapping: sig-evidence-index.pdf lists file-level mappings; attachments in first drop will include the checklist (segregation-checklist.xlsx) and the canonical diagram set. We'll upload to the Drive folder and set viewer permissions for Acme auditors.

- Operational call-outs: the only maintenance exception that materially affects routing is a scheduled rolling patch window (documented in runbook RUN-456). We can include sanitized runbook excerpts and change-ticket references if you need operational artifacts.

Deliverables attached below (first drop). If you want the on-prem airgap variant fully redacted for any sensitive internal hostnames, mention that and we'll provide sanitized label-only diagrams.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: segregation-checklist.xlsx, network-diagram-v3.png, sig-evidence-index.pdf
From: security@acme-fin.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_coole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ ask — Dedicated & Private network diagrams and isolation artifacts

Thanks Kimberly and Karthik — this is exactly what we need for the SIG intake. Two quick follow-ups before we close the loop: 

1) Could you include a short traffic flow table (source -> destination -> protocol/ports -> egress control) for the Private VPC-to-control-plane path? That will help our network team validate firewall rules.
2) Please confirm that the KV cache partitioning note is sufficient evidence for SIG scoping question SC-5 (no cross-tenant data leakage). If you can reference a test or smoke-check that was run (ticket ID or test run name), that will accelerate sign-off.

If you can drop the traffic flow table into the Drive folder by Monday morning (2026-08-03), we can proceed with the questionnaire review. Appreciate the staged delivery.

Regards,
Sara Patel
Senior Security Manager
Acme Financial
